## Oak Seedling Final Project DRAFT

### Summary Table

### Data Loading and Cleaning

In this section:

- reading in the data

- loading packages

- cleaning the data

```{r}
#loading packages to use in this project
library(tidyverse)
library(readxl)
library(dplyr)
```

```{r}
#reading in the soil moisture data 
Moist_Data_Raw <- 
  read_excel("Oak Data Entry MCRS Field Trip.xlsx", 
             sheet = "Soil Moisture")

#reading in the LICOR data
#thank you professor for putting the LICOR data read in code together 
LICOR_Data_Raw_NAMES <- 
  read_excel("Oak Data Entry MCRS Field Trip.xlsx",              
             sheet = "LICOR", 
             n_max = 3, 
             col_names = FALSE, 
             col_types = "text") |> 
  summarise(across(.fns = paste, collapse = "_")) |> 
  unlist() |> 
  unname()

LICOR_Data_Raw <- 
  read_excel("Oak Data Entry MCRS Field Trip.xlsx",  
             sheet = "LICOR", 
             skip = 3, 
             col_names = LICOR_Data_Raw_NAMES,
             col_types = "text")


ALL_Licor_NAMES <- 
  read_excel("Oak Data Entry MCRS Field Trip.xlsx", 
             sheet = "ALL_Licor_Ignore", 
             n_max = 3, 
             col_names = FALSE, 
             col_types = "text") |> 
  summarise(across(.fns = paste, collapse = "_")) |> 
  unlist() |> 
  unname()

ALL_Licor <- 
  read_excel("Oak Data Entry MCRS Field Trip.xlsx", 
             sheet = "ALL_Licor_Ignore", 
             skip = 3, 
             col_names = ALL_Licor_NAMES, 
             col_types = "text")

LICOR_Data_Raw <- full_join(LICOR_Data_Raw, ALL_Licor)

```

Cleaning the soil moisture data:

```{r}
Moist_Data_Raw #view the data so I remember what I need to do to clean it 

#First, I need to remove all of the excess NA values at the bottom 
Soil_Data <- Moist_Data_Raw |> 
  drop_na(Date) |> 
#Now, I am only interested in the date, block, treatment, and VWC% readings (three per block)
  select(Date, Block, Treatment, VWC1_perc, VWC2_perc, VWC3_perc) |> 
  #the VWC values are currently chr, and I need them in double format
  mutate(VWC1_perc= as.double(VWC1_perc)) |> 
  mutate(VWC2_perc = as.double(VWC2_perc)) |> 
  mutate(VWC3_perc = as.double(VWC3_perc)) |> 
  #Making date character so it'll work when I create a before/after column 
  mutate(Date = as.character(Date)) |> 
#Since I'm doing rain event, I want a before/after categorical variable
  mutate(Before_After = case_when(
    Date == "2026-10-08" ~ "Before",
    Date == "2026-10-21" ~ "After"
  ))


#now that Ive done all of that, I also realized that I need one VWC per treatment/block combo (so each row)

Soil_Data <- Soil_Data |> 
  rowwise() |> 
  mutate(Soil_VWC = mean(c(VWC1_perc , VWC2_perc, VWC3_perc), na.rm = TRUE))

```

Using this chunk to test that all of my data cleaning worked how I wanted it to, by making sure my graph works. This might be the graph I use later, idk

```{r}
Soil_Data |> 
  ggplot()+
  aes(x=Before_After, y= Soil_VWC)+
  geom_boxplot()
```

Now to clean the LICOR data (T.T)\

```{r}
LICOR_Data <- LICOR_Data_Raw |> 
  #remove excess rows of NA at bottom of sheet 
  drop_na(SYS_Date_YYYYMMDD) |> 
  #rename columns with too long names
  rename(Date = SYS_Date_YYYYMMDD) |> 
  rename(Block = `USERDEF_Block Number_NA`) |> 
  rename(Tag_Num = `USERDEF_Tag Number_NA` ) |> 
  rename(Treatment = Treatment_NA_NA) |> 
  rename(SapAB = Sapling_AB_etc_NA_NA) |> 
  rename(Survivorship = Dead_Alive_NA_NA) |> 
  rename(ETR = `FLUORO_ETR_umol+1m-2s-1`)
#the columns we renamed above are the only ones we are interested in, so I will select just those ones. 

LICOR_Data <- LICOR_Data |> 
  select(Date, Block, Tag_Num, Treatment, SapAB, Survivorship, ETR)

#A few more minor fixes
#First, some values are not in the format I want them in 
#Next, there are some rows with treatment as either NA or ??, neither of which are helpful. Since one of my vairables is treatment, if a row doesn't have treatment at all, it isn't useful to me, so I'm just going to remove it. 
LICOR_Data <- LICOR_Data |> 
  mutate(ETR = as.double(ETR)) |> 
  mutate(Tag_Num = as.factor(Tag_Num)) |> 
  drop_na(Treatment) |> 
  filter(Treatment != "??") |> 
  #Next, I need a B/A column for before after, since that is also one of the variables
  #Making date character so it'll work when I create a before/after column 
  mutate(Date = as.character(Date)) |> 
  #Since I'm doing rain event, I want a before/after categorical variable
  mutate(Before_After = case_when(
    Date == "2026-10-08" ~ "Before",
    Date == "2026-10-15" ~ "After"
  ))




```

```{r}
LICOR_Data
```

### ANOVA

Testing the following relationship: ETR \~ rain event \* habitat type

I want to test it with the interaction, as I expect the habitat type to have impacted how the rain water is received by the plant (the canopy/dead tree might keep it from getting as much rain, or might shield the soil from direct sunlight that would be causing evaporation).

In this section:

- Assumptions/ Normality tests

- ANOVA

- Figure

Tests before the ANOVA

```{r}
# Build the linear model
ETR_ANOVA_Model  <- lm(log(ETR)~ Treatment * Before_After, data = LICOR_Data)
#I did log(ETR) becuase the residuals of ETR looks crazy, this one looks a lot more normal 


plot(ETR_ANOVA_Model, which = 2)

# Create a QQ plot of residuals
ggpubr::ggqqplot(residuals(ETR_ANOVA_Model))
```

Next, test for the homogeneity of variance

```{r}
plot(ETR_ANOVA_Model, which = 1)

LICOR_Data |> 
  rstatix::levene_test(log(ETR) ~Treatment*Before_After )
#large p value means there is homogeneity of variance 
```

Now, we run the ANOVA

```{r}

#run the anova on the model
anova(ETR_ANOVA_Model)

```

From this we see that the Treatment and the relation to rain event (Before/After) were highly significant (TINY p-value), while the Treatment:Before_After (so the interaction) is significant (p-value = 0.015).

Now a graph! Let's do a boxplot, because those are cool

```{r}
 LICOR_Data |> 
   ggplot()+
   aes(x = Treatment, y = ETR)+
   geom_boxplot()+
   facet_wrap(Before_After)
 #IDK why this doesn't recognize the Before_After object, I'm 90% certain I have the syntax here right T.T 
```
